podcast.body: This was one of 20 songs played in 17 minutes during The Ramones' debut gig at CBGB on August 16, 1974. It quickly became one of the first songs to establish the "myth and cult" of The Ramones, embodying their sound of bubblegum pop mixed with 60s garage rock played at high speed. "They played 20 songs in 17 minutes, including this one. Blitzkrieg Bob, one of the first songs to figure into the myth and cult of the Ramones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song, released in 1976, is characteristic of The Ramones' signature sound: raw and ragged, it delivered 60s bubblegum pop melodies with the volume and speed of a jet engine. The track further cemented their status as the "ultimate punks" through both their sound and image. "The leather jacketed raw and ragged at Ramones with Blitzkrieg Bop from 1976."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song, with its iconic "Hey Ho, Let's Go" opening, was The Ramones' first single from their debut album in early 1976. The opening chant was an homage to the Bay City Rollers' "Saturday Night," and Joey Ramone sang this part, though D.D. and Tommy Ramone wrote the song. "So that, hey, oh, let's go, you know, that fun opening with Blitzkrieg Bop And that's the Ramones homage to the Bassity Rollers And that is in fact Joey Ramone singing out that, hey, oh, part, although D.D. and Tommy Ramone wrote it."

"The Ramones, with Blitzkrieg Bop from 1976, a song inspired in part by the chanting of a big hit of the day, was by the Bay City Rollers."
